title: A Survey of AIOps in the Era of Large Language Models
authors: Lingzhe Zhang; Tong Jia; Mengxi Jia; Yifan Wu; Aiwei Liu; Yong Yang; Zhonghai Wu; Xuming Hu; Philip Yu; Ying Li
venue: ACM Computing Surveys
summary: Surveys 183 papers from 2020-2024 on using large language models for AIOps, analysing data sources, task evolution, LLM-based methods and evaluation practices.
method: Systematic literature review (four research questions)
key_result: Maps how LLMs reshape failure data processing and enable new AIOps tasks such as incident summarisation and agent-based root-cause analysis.
limitation_or_critique: Focused on software/cloud operations; telecom core networks and standardised analytics functions are essentially absent from the reviewed corpus.

title: Fault Prediction for Heterogeneous Telecommunication Networks Using Machine Learning: A Survey
authors: Killian Murphy; Antoine Lavignotte; Catherine Lepers
venue: IEEE Transactions on Network and Service Management
summary: Telecom-specific survey of machine-learning network fault prediction, framed from the viewpoint of a network and system integrator handling heterogeneous equipment.
method: Literature survey plus a cost-oriented evaluation metric
key_result: Introduces a metric measuring expected maintenance-cost reduction from a predictive model and gives recommendations for ML use in telecom fault prediction.
limitation_or_critique: Equipment-level fault prediction dominates; cloud-native 5G core functions and 3GPP NWDAF/MDAF analytics are not a central focus.

title: Anomaly Detection and Failure Root Cause Analysis in (Micro) Service-Based Cloud Applications: A Survey
authors: Jacopo Soldani; Antonio Brogi
venue: ACM Computing Surveys
summary: Structured qualitative survey classifying anomaly-detection and root-cause-analysis techniques for multi-service cloud applications by the observability data they consume (logs, metrics, traces).
method: Literature survey and taxonomy
key_result: Provides a taxonomy that separates detection from RCA techniques and lists open challenges for microservice-based systems.
limitation_or_critique: Covers generic cloud applications only and predates both LLM-based RCA and telecom-specific cloud-native network functions.

title: A Survey of AIOps Methods for Failure Management
authors: Paolo Notaro; Jorge Cardoso; Michael Gerndt
venue: ACM Transactions on Intelligent Systems and Technology
summary: Reviews about one hundred AIOps failure-management solutions and organises them into five categories and fourteen subcategories according to their intervention time window.
method: Systematic literature review
key_result: Proposes a reference taxonomy (failure prevention, prediction, detection, root-cause analysis, remediation) widely reused in later AIOps work.
limitation_or_critique: IT-operations oriented, with no treatment of telecom network functions or of 3GPP management analytics.

title: 5GC-Trace-RCA: Distributed Tracing-Based Root Cause Analysis for QoS Troubleshooting in Cloud Native 5G Core Network
authors: Anping Zhao; Frederic Desnoes; Ilhem Fajjari; Nadjib Aitsaadi
venue: NOMS 2026-2026 IEEE Network Operations and Management Symposium
summary: Proposes an end-to-end RCA architecture that builds anomaly propagation chains from causal relations in distributed traces of cloud-native 5G core procedures.
method: Distributed tracing + causal anomaly propagation chains
data_or_testbed: Real 5G traffic from a macro-cell at Paris-Charles de Gaulle airport
key_result: Localises diverse service failures and performance degradations across 5GC NFs and improves root-cause precision by exposing cascading effects.
limitation_or_critique: One of very few RCA works on real 5GC traffic, but tracing instrumentation of the core is assumed and generality beyond the studied deployment is not shown.

title: MDAF-Based Explainable Failure Prediction for Network Functions in 5G/6G
authors: Sukhyun Nam; Wonseok Choi; James Won-Ki Hong
venue: NOMS 2026-2026 IEEE Network Operations and Management Symposium
summary: Implements a 3GPP-style Management Data Analytics Function that predicts and explains NF failures using multi-domain metrics and logs, a CNV-GRU time-series predictor, SHAP attributions and LLM explanations.
method: CNV-GRU with focal loss + SHAP + LLM natural-language reasoning
key_result: Reaches up to 78.6% F1 for detection, 73.0% for 3-minute-ahead prediction and 77.8% accuracy in naming the responsible NF.
limitation_or_critique: Rare explicit MDAF implementation, but accuracy levels remain modest and evaluation is limited to one open-source testbed.

title: Deep Learning-Based Proactive Anomaly Detection for 5G Core Control Plane Network Function Interactions
authors: Yawen Tan; Jiajia Liu; Yuanhao Li; Jiadai Wang
venue: IEEE Transactions on Cognitive Communications and Networking
summary: Proposes 5GCGuard, a deep sequence model that learns normal NF-to-NF service interaction patterns in the SBA control plane and flags deviations as anomalies.
method: Attention-based sequence model with multi-task learning, probabilistic labelling and automatic thresholding
key_result: Outperforms comparison schemes on the testbed and, in case studies, proactively detects several kinds of abnormal NF interactions.
limitation_or_critique: Evaluated on a single self-built testbed with injected attack scenarios, so transfer to multi-vendor operational cores is unproven and root-cause localisation is not addressed.

title: Granomaly: A Framework for Anomaly Detection in 5G Core Network Control Plane Traffic with Temporal Graph Neural Networks
authors: Tobias Fritz; Alexander Schwankner; Jan-Hendrik Wissing; Robin Buchta; Gabi Dreo Rodosek
venue: NOMS 2025-2025 IEEE Network Operations and Management Symposium
summary: Represents 5G core control-plane traffic as a temporal graph and applies temporal graph neural networks to detect subtle anomalies, positioning the approach alongside NWDAF analytics.
method: Temporal graph neural networks (two TGNN variants)
data_or_testbed: Simulated 5G core; two benchmark datasets released
key_result: Shows that TGNNs detect subtle control-plane traffic anomalies and contributes two TGNN-ready benchmark datasets.
limitation_or_critique: Relies on a simulated core and security-style anomalies, and leaves integration with a real NWDAF and root-cause localisation open.

title: Modality-Agnostic Root Cause Analysis with Optimal Transport for 5G Core Network
authors: Nobukazu Fukuda; Haruhisa Nozue; Kenichi Tayama
venue: GLOBECOM 2025 - 2025 IEEE Global Communications Conference
summary: Proposes an unsupervised, entity-centric RCA method for 5G core failures that compares telemetry distributions with optimal transport, so it works when some data modalities are missing.
method: Optimal transport on heterogeneous telemetry (metrics, logs, packets) keyed to entities
data_or_testbed: 5G core connected to an IP backbone (operator lab)
key_result: Improves RCA accuracy over baselines under both complete and partial observability.
limitation_or_critique: Lab-scale evaluation by a single operator group; no comparison with standardised analytics outputs such as NWDAF or MDA reports.

title: 5G Core Fault Detection and Root Cause Analysis using Machine Learning and Generative AI
authors: Joseph H. R. Isaac; Harish Saradagam; Nallamothu Pardhasaradhi
venue: arXiv preprint
summary: Describes a fault-analysis engine that classifies faulty frames in 5G packet-core PCAP and log test files with NLP models and uses an LLM grounded in 3GPP and product documents to suggest fixes.
method: NLP classifiers on PCAP frames + document-grounded LLM for remediation hints
key_result: Reports high frame-classification accuracy with an 80-20 split and LLM-generated domain explanations of errors.
limitation_or_critique: Preprint (accepted at a small conference) targeting test-lab artefacts rather than live operations; LLM explanation quality is not rigorously evaluated.

title: Fault Diagnosis Using Hybrid Transfer Learning for VNF-based 5G Core Networks
authors: Tianhao Zhu; Yoshiaki Narusue; Hiroyuki Morikawa
venue: 2024 IEEE Conference on Network Function Virtualization and Software Defined Networks (NFV-SDN)
summary: Combines model-, instance- and feature-based transfer learning to move fault-diagnosis knowledge from a scale-out 5G testbed to a real 5G core with little labelled data.
method: Hybrid transfer learning for fault classification across VNFs
key_result: Hybrid transfer learning beats no-transfer and plain model-based transfer, with 70% of fault labels reaching F1 above 0.9.
limitation_or_critique: Addresses the important data-scarcity problem, but the target network is small and the fault taxonomy is limited to predefined classes.

title: A Method of Alarm Correlation and Root Cause Analysis in 5G Core Network
authors: Shiyu Zhou; Xiqing Liu; Xinzhou Cheng; Zhenqiao Zhao; Jingyun Wang; Tian Xiao
venue: Lecture Notes in Electrical Engineering
summary: Proposes alarm correlation and root-cause analysis for an operator 5G core by combining an expert-built rule base with graph neural networks.
method: Expert rules + GNN-based alarm correlation
key_result: Authors claim substantial gains in operation and maintenance efficiency; detailed quantitative results were not visible to us.
limitation_or_critique: Short proceedings chapter whose full evaluation could not be checked; rule-base dependence limits portability across vendors.

title: ADSeq-5GCN: Anomaly Detection from Network Traffic Sequences in 5G Core Network Control Plane
authors: Zixu Tian; Rajendra Patil; Mohan Gurusamy; Joshua McCloud
venue: 2023 IEEE 24th International Conference on High Performance Switching and Routing (HPSR)
summary: Models captured 5G core control-plane traffic as sequences of service events and uses a Bi-LSTM to predict the next event, treating mispredictions as anomalies.
method: Bi-LSTM next-event prediction on NF-to-NF traffic
key_result: Reports clearly better detection than baseline models across several attack and misbehaviour scenarios on the free5GC testbed.
limitation_or_critique: Testbed-scale evaluation centred on hostile-NF scenarios; it detects but does not localise or explain faults.

title: Deep Learning-Based Log Anomaly Detection for 5G Core Network
authors: Yawen Tan; Jiadai Wang; Jiajia Liu; Yuanhao Li
venue: 2023 IEEE/CIC International Conference on Communications in China (ICCC)
summary: Builds a modular deep-learning log anomaly detection pipeline (parsing, grouping, feature extraction, training) for internal failures of a virtualised 5G core.
method: Log parsing + deep learning classifiers
data_or_testbed: Cloud-native 5G testbed with injected anomalies (own log dataset)
key_result: Best configuration exceeds 97% F1 on the collected 5G core log dataset.
limitation_or_critique: Log dataset comes from one open-source core implementation with synthetic fault injection, and the work stops at detection without root-cause attribution.

title: Failure Prediction in Cloud Native 5G Core With eBPF-based Observability
authors: Junichi Kawasaki; Daiki Koyama; Takuya Miyasaka; Tomohiro Otani
venue: 2023 IEEE 97th Vehicular Technology Conference (VTC2023-Spring)
summary: Uses eBPF to collect fine-grained infrastructure data under cloud-native network functions and trains an LSTM to forecast KPI trajectories for failure prediction in a 5G core.
method: eBPF telemetry + LSTM KPI forecasting
key_result: Models trained with eBPF-derived features predict better than models trained without them.
limitation_or_critique: Lab experiment with limited failure types; prediction is not linked to root-cause localisation or automated remediation.

title: Graph-based Interpretable Anomaly Detection Framework for Network Slice Management in Beyond 5G Networks
authors: Ashima Chawla; Anne-Marie Bosneag; Anestis Dalgkitsis
venue: NOMS 2023-2023 IEEE/IFIP Network Operations and Management Symposium
summary: Presents G5IAD, which models correlations among multivariate network-slice KPIs with graph convolutions and GRU forecasting to detect and explain slice-level anomalies.
method: GCN + GRU forecasting + probabilistic anomaly classification
key_result: Provides unsupervised, interpretable slice-level anomaly detection intended to speed up root-cause analysis for self-managed slices.
limitation_or_critique: Simulation-based evaluation; explanation is at KPI-feature level rather than identification of the faulty NF.

title: Large Language Models (LLMs) for Telecom Root Cause Analysis (RCA): A Structured Reasoning Framework for Evidence-Grounded Diagnosis
authors: Hao Zhou; Mandar Kulkarni; Hao Chen; Yan Xin; Charlie Jianzhong Zhang
venue: IEEE Wireless Communications
summary: Reviews the evolution of telecom RCA toward LLM-enabled techniques and proposes a structured, evidence-grounded reasoning framework to curb hallucination in LLM diagnosis.
method: Canonical telemetry contexts + enforced decision-path reasoning with LLMs
key_result: Improves diagnostic accuracy and decision consistency over baseline LLM techniques on both datasets.
limitation_or_critique: Magazine-style article; the datasets are mainly radio-performance troubleshooting rather than core NF faults.

title: Root Cause Analysis for Microservice System based on Causal Inference: How Far Are We?
authors: Luan Pham; Huong Ha; Hongyu Zhang
venue: Proceedings of the 39th IEEE/ACM International Conference on Automated Software Engineering
summary: Benchmarks nine causal-discovery and twenty-one causal-inference RCA methods for microservices on synthetic and real-system datasets.
method: Large-scale empirical comparison
data_or_testbed: Synthetic datasets and benchmark microservice systems
key_result: Finds that no method dominates and that results on synthetic data poorly predict performance on real systems.
limitation_or_critique: Valuable reality check, but restricted to IT microservices; telecom-specific fault propagation through 3GPP procedures is untested.

title: Automatic Root Cause Analysis via Large Language Models for Cloud Incidents
authors: Yinfang Chen; Huaibing Xie; Minghua Ma; Yu Kang; Xin Gao; Liu Shi; Yunjie Cao; Xuedong Gao; Hao Fan; Ming Wen; Jun Zeng; Supriyo Ghosh; Xuchao Zhang; Chaoyun Zhang; Qingwei Lin; Saravan Rajmohan; Dongmei Zhang; Tianyin Xu
venue: Proceedings of the Nineteenth European Conference on Computer Systems
summary: Presents RCACopilot, an LLM-powered on-call system that routes incidents to handlers, gathers diagnostic data, predicts root-cause categories and writes explanations.
method: Incident handlers + LLM root-cause category prediction and explanation
data_or_testbed: One year of Microsoft production incidents
key_result: Reaches RCA accuracy up to 0.766 on real incidents, and its data-collection component has been in production for years.
limitation_or_critique: Proprietary data and cloud-service incident types; requires curated handlers, so porting to telecom operations would need domain workflows.

title: RCAgent: Cloud Root Cause Analysis by Autonomous Agents with Tool-Augmented Large Language Models
authors: Zefan Wang; Zichuan Liu; Yingying Zhang; Aoxiao Zhong; Jihong Wang; Fengbin Yin; Lunting Fan; Lingfei Wu; Qingsong Wen
venue: Proceedings of the 33rd ACM International Conference on Information and Knowledge Management
summary: Proposes a tool-augmented autonomous LLM agent for privacy-aware industrial RCA that collects data and analyses it freely, with trajectory-level self-consistency and context management.
method: ReAct-style tool-using LLM agent with self-consistency over action trajectories
key_result: Consistently outperforms ReAct on root cause, solution, evidence and responsibility prediction, and is deployed in production diagnosis.
limitation_or_critique: Evaluated on one cloud platform with internal models; safety of agent actions in a live network is not studied.

title: Eadro: An End-to-End Troubleshooting Framework for Microservices on Multi-source Data
authors: Cheryl Lee; Tianyi Yang; Zhuangbin Chen; Yuxin Su; Michael R. Lyu
venue: 2023 IEEE/ACM 45th International Conference on Software Engineering (ICSE)
summary: Jointly learns anomaly detection and root-cause localisation from traces, logs and KPIs by modelling intra-service behaviour and inter-service dependencies.
method: Multi-modal deep learning with graph modelling of service dependencies
data_or_testbed: Microservice benchmark systems with fault injection
key_result: Shows that coupling detection and localisation on multi-source data outperforms single-source, two-stage pipelines.
limitation_or_critique: Supervised and trained on benchmark applications; label availability in operator networks is a practical obstacle.

title: Digital-Twin assisted Root Cause Analysis of Anomalies in NFV Environment
authors: Weili Wang; Qianbin Chen; Tong Liu; Lun Tang
venue: ICC 2021 - IEEE International Conference on Communications
summary: Uses a digital twin to maintain a real-time anomaly-fault dependency matrix in NFV and solves root-cause localisation as a dynamic set-covering problem with parallel hidden Markov models.
method: Digital twin + HMM-based dynamic set covering solved with ADMM
key_result: Simulations show the distributed digital-twin assisted RCA identifies minimal faulty-component sets better than compared methods.
limitation_or_critique: Simulation-only and focused on VM/server faults rather than 5G core NF procedures.

title: MicroRCA: Root Cause Localization of Performance Issues in Microservices
authors: Li Wu; Johan Tordsson; Erik Elmroth; Odej Kao
venue: NOMS 2020 - 2020 IEEE/IFIP Network Operations and Management Symposium
summary: Locates root causes of microservice performance issues by building an attributed graph linking services and hosts and ranking candidates via anomaly propagation, without application instrumentation.
method: Attributed graph + personalised PageRank-style propagation
data_or_testbed: Microservice benchmark on Kubernetes with injected faults
key_result: Reports 89% precision and 97% mean average precision, ahead of earlier methods.
limitation_or_critique: Widely used baseline, but limited to metric data and a single benchmark application; telecom NFs are not evaluated.
